_global: Gravity: the Moon has 1/6 of Earth's gravity, so traction, dust behaviour and landing loads differ everywhere on Earth.
Vacuum: no Earth site removes the atmosphere, which scatters light, carries heat and slows dust.
Radiation: Earth's magnetic field and air block the radiation crews and electronics face on the Moon.
Temperature: the lunar south pole ranges from deep cryogenic cold in permanent shadow to well above freezing in sunlight; no Earth site comes close (see the temperature bar).
Regolith and dust: lunar soil is sharp, electrostatically charged and unweathered; Earth surfaces are eroded by wind and water.
Scale: these scores use 30 m pixels, so they describe landscape-scale terrain (landing zones, routes), not single rocks under a wheel.

haughton.why: Best-known Moon/Mars analog; high-latitude impact crater.

sp_crater.why: NASA Desert RATS test area; volcanic cone and lava flows.

meteor_crater.why: Classic impact-crater training site for Apollo astronauts.

mauna_kea.why: Volcanic terrain used for lunar resource (ISRU) tests.

svalbard.why: Used for Mars tests; never scored for lunar low-sun lighting.

peary_land.why: Ice-free polar desert at very high latitude.

dry_valleys.why: Ice-free ground with months of low sun.

khaybar.why: Large basalt field with lava tubes.

kamil.why: Pristine 45 m impact crater, like the small fresh craters rovers meet on the Moon.

black_desert.why: Hills capped with dark basalt and dolerite; reachable by road from Cairo.

gilf_kebir.why: Steep scarps and cliffs for slope testing.
